function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is a formal authorization that a client gives to a financial institution (or another party) to carry out specific actions on their behalf. Think of it as a written “instruction” that tells the bank or service provider exactly what they’re allowed to do with your money. ### Key points | Aspect | What it means | |--------|---------------| | **Purpose** | Gives the institution permission to act for you – e.g., transfer funds, pay bills, or manage investments. | | **Typical forms** | • **Standing order** – a regular payment you set up.
• **Direct debit** – a recurring withdrawal authorized by you.
• **Payment mandate** – a one‑time or scheduled instruction to move money. | | **Why it matters** | • Enables automated, repeatable transactions without needing manual approval each time.
• Provides legal clarity: the institution knows exactly what it’s allowed to do. | | **Status** | Mandates can be *active* (currently valid), *pending* (awaiting confirmation), or *inactive* (cancelled/expired). | ### How it shows up in our system When you call the `partner_mandates` or `user_mandates` functions, you’re asking the API to list the mandates that exist for a partner or a particular user. You can filter by status (`active`, `pending`, `inactive`) to see only those that are currently in effect, awaiting activation, or no longer valid. In short, a mandate is the official, often legally binding, permission that lets a bank or service perform transactions on your behalf.
